diagram_math_checks.justification: Use S={s1,s2}, three actions with immediate reward vectors (1,0), (0,1), (1/5,1/5), horizon 1, and b=(1-p,p) for p in [0,1]. Such finite deterministic rewards are allowed by F1. Proof step 1.1 has Gamma_0={0}; F3/step 2.1 then returns exactly the three reward vectors, independently of transition and observation kernels.

The local representation in step 4.1 gives b dot alpha_1=1-p, b dot alpha_2=p, b dot alpha_3=1/5. Plot coordinates use x=6p and y=3 times value, so candidate segments are (0,3) to (6,0), (0,0) to (6,3), and y=0.6.

1-p=p iff p=1/2. For p<=1/2, 1-p>=p, and for p>=1/2, p>=1-p. In either case the maximum is >=1/2>1/5. Hence thick segments (0,3)--(3,1.5)--(6,3) are exactly V_1. Witness regions are the closed intervals [0,1/2] and [1/2,1], with both vectors witnessed at the tie; alpha_3 has no witness, matching statement and steps 5.1/5.3.

Both endpoint beliefs p=0 and p=1 are in the simplex; filled circles mark these included endpoints, and the central filled circle marks the included tie. There are no open endpoints, transition arrows, or commutative-map claims. The thick graph is an open two-segment chain with three vertices and degrees 1,2,1; no closing edge is required. Only coordinate axes carry arrowheads.
The complete numbered proof, including envelope/convexity/witness arguments in steps 5.1–5.3, is unchanged and does not invoke the figure.
